perspective:
From Gloria Bangura’s perspective:

- I am an administrative assistant at a large event planning company, and Donald Ortega is a part-time bartender there during events. We’re colleagues, but not personally close.
- Over several company events, I noticed Donald seemed distracted and lacked enthusiasm while serving drinks.
- I approached him and asked if everything was okay with the job. He told me he wasn’t as into it as he used to be and that it felt repetitive.
- After thinking about it more, I wondered if his job dissatisfaction might be connected to something deeper going on in his life.
- I suggested he consider talking to a professional about it. He said he hadn’t really considered that and wasn’t sure it would help.
- Afterward, I sensed a change in his behavior toward me and worried he might have resented my suggestion or felt I overstepped.
- I apologized to him and said I only meant to help because I cared. He said he was a bit taken aback at first but knew I meant well, and that it was a lot to process.
- Relieved that the tension seemed to ease, I invited him to collaborate on a new project, saying it could use his creative input. He thanked me and agreed, saying it sounded like a great opportunity.
- During the project, I observed his significant contributions and renewed enthusiasm.
- I publicly acknowledged his work in a team meeting and said his efforts were crucial to our success.
- He thanked me, said it meant a lot to him, and expressed that he was glad to contribute and felt appreciated.
